Subject: INTERNAL: Citrine sizing draft + proposed switchover map

Team — Elena sent high-level traffic description (attached request samples expected today). Based on initial questions and similar deals, I sketched two candidate capacity profiles:

1) Conservative (SLA-first): 8xA100-80GB equiv in a dedicated pool (reserve 25% headroom). Assumes single-model worst-case BKTR.
2) Optimized (cost-first): 6xA100 with aggressive batching + quantized weights (8-bit) + prefix cache; expected token cost reduction ~38% but requires an additional QA pass and fallback policy.

Key acceptance checkpoints we should commit to in the runbook:
- Traffic ingest & replay (RD 1): 2/3 day post-sample for sim results
- Throughput validation (RD 2): 4-hour stress window with synthetic spikes to 150% planned peak
- Canary (RD 3): 2-hour live canary with 5% routed traffic and full tracing enabled
- Full swap (RD 4): 4-hour blackout with staged route flip and automatic rollback on error thresholds

Proposed timeline (subject to attachments and DocuSign):
- 2026-11-24: Traf samples received (confirmed expected)
- 2026-11-29: Simulation results + draft sizing (deliverable to customer)
- 2026-12-06: Sign commitment (target)
- 2026-12-15 to 2026-12-22: GPU provisioning and staging activation
- 2027-01-10: Preflight replay + acceptance window (RD1/RD2)
- 2027-01-17: Canary and monitored 48hr window (RD3)
- 2027-01-24: Full swap (RD4)

Notes / asks:
- Karthik: can you prepare a quick baseline throughput sim for the two profiles? Include 95th/99th latency.
- Soojin: CS will need acceptance criteria doc & rollback checklist; can you draft?
- Jordan: Ops lead for cutover on the day — agree to be on call?

I attached a quick commit_summary pdf (stub) and will add the traffic sample once NDA is signed.

Thanks,
Priya

Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Citrine sizing draft + proposed switchover map

Folks — did a quick back-of-envelope and a small sim with representative prompts. Main points:
- Baseline (no quant): 8xA100 required to hold 120M tokens/day with 25% burst capacity and maintain 95th token latency <220ms. Peak session concurrency modeled at 600 rps.
- With 8-bit quant + continuous batching + 256-token KV cache hit rate 40%: we can push that to 6xA100 and hit median token latency target ~110-140ms, 95th ~200ms.
- Danger cases: multimodal prompts (long context >4k tokens) or large system prompts cause KV invalidation and spike memory; we should include per-model sequence-length SLAs in acceptance.

Technical asks for customer artifacts:
- Tokenization sample + 72-hour trace with timestamps
- A list of top-50 prompt families (for caching opportunities)
- Any PII redaction constraints that affect batching logic

I opened RED-3821 for an internal checklist (throughput sim, kernel selection, canary alarms). I attached throughput-sim.csv with the scenarios I ran.

Karthik
Infra Lead, Serving Runtime

Elena / Victor — thanks for the signed DocuSign and the traces. Below is the agreed plan; I’ll publish a runbook to the HubSpot deal and create RED-3821 subtask for the canary.

Runbook highlights and dates (final):
- 2026-11-24: Customer traces received (complete)
- 2026-11-29: Redwood: deliver simulation + two capacity profiles (Conservative: 8xA100; Optimized: 6xA100 with quant).
- 2026-12-06: Signed commitment (completed).
- 2026-12-15 to 2026-12-22: Dedicated pool provisioning + staging activation. Ops will run a dry smoke test (internal).
- 2027-01-10: Preflight: 4-hour replay + 95/99 latency report (customer acceptance).
- 2027-01-17: Canary: 2-hour 5% live traffic with full tracing. Acceptance gates: no regression >5% in median latency, no more than 1% error rate, and token-cost delta within agreed tolerance.
- 2027-01-24 (02:00-06:00 PT): Full swap window (target). Rollback policy: automated route flipback to hosted if error thresholds exceeded for >30 minutes. Emergency fallback: maintain hot hosted path for 10% traffic for 72 hours post-swap.
